Q: How can I create virtual env with Python 3? A:

Use:

python3 -m venv ./path-to-new-venv

This is the recommended way to create virtual environments.

Historically, a wrapper command pyvenv was provided for this. However, the wrapper was deprecated in Python 3.6, and removed in 3.8.

Q: How to get a value from another table if one table doesn't return any value - plsql A:

One option is to UNION selects from both tables, using exists (while selecting from testa) and not exists (when selecting from testb).

Initially, both tables have data which means that query should select only from testa:

SQL> insert into testa values (1, 2, 3);

1 row created.

SQL> insert into testb values (100, 200, 300);

1 row created.

Query:

SQL> select *
  2  from testa
  3  where exists (select null
  4                from testa
  5               )
  6  union
  7  select *
  8  from testb
  9  where not exists (select null
 10                    from testa
 11                   );

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
         1           2          3       --> this belongs to TESTA table

Let's delete row(s) from testa:

SQL> delete from testa;

1 row deleted.

Try again; result should now come from testb:

SQL> select *
  2  from testa
  3  where exists (select null
  4                from testa
  5               )
  6  union
  7  select *
  8  from testb
  9  where not exists (select null
 10                    from testa
 11                   );

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
       100         200        300    --> really, this belongs to TESTB

SQL>

As you tagged the question with plsql tag, let's switch to it:

SQL> create or replace procedure p_test is
  2  begin
  3    for cur_r in (
  4            select *
  5          from testa
  6          where exists (select null
  7                        from testa
  8                       )
  9          union
 10          select *
 11          from testb
 12          where not exists (select null
 13                            from testa
 14                           )
 15    ) loop
 16      dbms_output.put_line(cur_r.inquiry_no);
 17    end loop;
 18  end;
 19  /

Procedure created.

Initial sample data:

SQL> set serveroutput on
SQL> truncate table testa;

Table truncated.

SQL> truncate table testb;

Table truncated.

SQL> insert into testa values (1, 2, 3);

1 row created.

SQL> insert into testb values (100, 200, 300);

1 row created.

Testing:

SQL> exec p_test;
1                             --> this is from TESTA

PL/SQL procedure successfully completed.

SQL> delete from testa;

1 row deleted.

SQL> exec p_test;
100                          --> this is from TESTB

PL/SQL procedure successfully completed.

SQL>

[EDIT], based on additional explanation and sample data with desired result.

SQL> select * from testa;

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
         1           2          3

SQL> select * From testb;

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
       100         200        300

Slightly modified query, which searches for inquiry_no in both tables. not exists eliminates rows from testb if they exist in testa.

SQL> with temp as
  2    (
  3      select *
  4      from testa
  5      where inquiry_no = &&par_inquiry_no
  6      union
  7      select *
  8      from testb
  9      where not exists (select null
 10                        from testa
 11                        where inquiry_no = &&par_inquiry_no
 12                       )
 13        and inquiry_no = &&par_inquiry_no
 14    )
 15  select *
 16  from temp;

Testing:

Enter value for par_inquiry_no: 1

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
         1           2          3

SQL> undefine par_inquiry_no
SQL> /
Enter value for par_inquiry_no: 100

INQUIRY_NO REVISION_NO      TOTAL
---------- ----------- ----------
       100         200        300

SQL> undefine par_inquiry_no
SQL> /
Enter value for par_inquiry_no: 11

no rows selected

SQL>

Q: Is there any way to perform a pivot on a Polars LazyFrame? A:

polars.LazyFrame.pivot is now available, starting from Python Polars 1.36.0 (2025/12). This is the pull request which created it.

Please notice that the argument on_columns is required.

import polars as pl

df = pl.from_repr("""
┌──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬───────────┬───────┐
│ ind1 ┆ ind2 ┆ ind3 ┆ ind4 ┆ my_signal ┆ Value │
│ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---   │
│ str  ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str       ┆ i64   │
╞══════╪══════╪══════╪══════╪═══════════╪═══════╡
│ www  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ a         ┆ 1     │
│ www  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ a         ┆ 1     │
│ www  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ a         ┆ 1     │
│ www  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ b         ┆ 2     │
│ fff  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ b         ┆ 2     │
│ fff  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ b         ┆ 2     │
│ fff  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ c         ┆ 3     │
│ fff  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ c         ┆ 3     │
│ fff  ┆ xxx  ┆ yyy  ┆ zzz  ┆ c         ┆ 3     │
└──────┴──────┴──────┴──────┴───────────┴───────┘
""")

# DataFrame
df.pivot("my_signal", values="Value", aggregate_function="mean")

# LazyFrame
df_lf = df.lazy()
df_lf.pivot(
    "my_signal", on_columns=["a", "b", "c"], values="Value", aggregate_function="mean"
)

If you don't know what to put as "on_columns", you can still collect unique values of the column, it should not be too costfull :


new_cols = df_lf.select(pl.col("my_signal").unique()).collect().get_column("my_signal").to_list()
df_lf.pivot(
    "my_signal", on_columns=new_cols, values="Value", aggregate_function="mean"
)```

Q: How can the default Node.js version be set using NVM? A:

The current answers did not solve the problem for me, because I had Node.js installed in /usr/bin/node and /usr/local/bin/node, so the system always resolved these first, and ignored the nvm version.

I solved the issue by moving the existing versions to /usr/bin/node-system and /usr/local/bin/node-system.

Then I didn't have any node command anymore, until I used nvm use :(

I solved this issue by creating a symbolic link to the version that would be installed by nvm.

sudo mv /usr/local/bin/node /usr/local/bin/node-system
sudo mv /usr/bin/node /usr/bin/node-system
nvm use node
  # Now using node v12.20.1 (npm v6.14.10)

which node
  # /home/paul/.nvm/versions/node/v12.20.1/bin/node
sudo ln -s /home/paul/.nvm/versions/node/v12.20.1/bin/node /usr/bin/node

Then open a new shell

node -v

Output:

  v12.20.1

Q: Add days to day-of-week, in Java. Ex: Sunday + 2 = Tuesday A:

tl;dr

java.time.DayOfWeek.SUNDAY.plus( 2 ) ➡️ DayOfWeek.TUESDAY

DayOfWeek enum

You said:

ArrayList which contains every day of the week

No need. Java 8+ comes with a the java.time.DayOfWeek enum, with predefined objects for each day of the week.

You can add days to reach another day-of-week. And the week wraps around when adding.

It also needs to be able to "loop around", so if the current day is Sunday and the value is 2, it should return Tuesday.

Built-in feature.

DayOfWeek dow = DayOfWeek.SUNDAY.plus( 2L );

TUESDAY
